A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAPo work, and their supplied text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. However, both end with references and omit the appendices they explicitly cite, preventing comparison of deferred implementation details and supplementary experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAPo reconstruction results on N3DV and Meet Room, computational measurements, and component ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and reports additional baseline, temporal-consistency, and partition-depth results in Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same deformation architecture, displacement/variance dynamic score, recursive temporal partitioning, static Gaussian conversion, and cross-frame losses. Newly disclosed hyperparameters and additional experimental controls do not establish a change to MAPo's procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate N3DV and Meet Room under the same reconstruction task. The broader Meet Room ablation and flame_salmon_frag3 depth study use already represented data; they introduce no distinct dataset, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add LocalDyGS and E-D3DGS (seg), retaining the existing comparators. Table 3 also adds the segmentation baseline. These are targeted additions, including a useful control comparing adaptive partitioning with uniform temporal slicing.

E3.justification: The component-evaluation design is substantially expanded: Table 3 changes from Vrheadset-only results to Meet Room results, with resource measurements on discussion, and adds whole-video and partition-boundary tOF evaluation. New protocols include three independently trained segments for E-D3DGS (seg) and a partition-level sweep from 0 to 5. Main benchmark resolutions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a naive-slicing control, quantitative boundary-consistency analysis, and a partition-depth sensitivity study examining quality versus computational cost (Tables 3–4). Figure 9 expands the existing quality illustration into consecutive frames across a partition boundary, providing additional evidence about the consistency loss.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added average and boundary tOF values are evaluation metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes MAPo's N3DV PSNR from 31.26 to 31.33 and SSIM from 0.943 to 0.944. Table 2 changes 4DGaussians' training time from 14 to 63 minutes and FPS from 31.98 to 77.26. Added baseline results, replacement of the single-scene ablation with Meet Room results, new tOF measurements, and Table 4 substantially expand the evidence. The replacement ablation scores are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the mathematical definitions of deformation, dynamic scoring, partitioning, and consistency losses are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is supplied; tOF is introduced as an evaluation metric.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly frame reconstruction as using multi-view video inputs, narrowing the previously generic problem description. The central partitioning and consistency-loss contributions, superior rendering-quality claim, and competitive-efficiency claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the segmentation control as evidence that adaptive partitioning offers benefits beyond naive slicing. It explains diminishing quality returns beyond partition level 3 and uses that trade-off to justify the chosen depth. The continuity discussion also strengthens its conclusion to completely mitigating the boundary issue based on the added tOF results.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly specifies 300 recorded historical positions and maximum partition level 3. These are additional disclosures, not demonstrated changes from v1's settings. Both versions identify the E-D3DGS codebase and RTX A6000 hardware, while deferring further implementation details to unavailable appendices.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for LocalDyGS and Scaffold-GS, cites temporal Gaussian hierarchy work, and adds Chu et al. as the source for tOF. The broader positioning against unified deformation models and window-based partitioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 introduces numbered subsections, changes citation style, edits introductory and related-work passages, condenses the quantitative discussion and conclusion, and expands the ablation narrative. The same six main sections and overall argument are retained.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different title block, heading styles, caption placement, and figure/table positioning. Figure 1 replaces its example, Figure 9 becomes an annotated frame-sequence comparison, Table 3 gains a control row and temporal-metric column, and Table 4 is added. Most other illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's qualitative continuity evidence and single-scene component ablation, v2 provides quantitative boundary measurements, a relevant naive-slicing control, broader ablations, and a depth-versus-cost study. These strengthen validation and parameter transparency. The method and main conclusions remain stable, while the missing referenced appendices continue to limit reproducibility.
